fields.System.Title: RET-3 — Inspection
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Assess what actually came back, record the assessment, and gate everything downstream on it.

Scope

In. Recording an inspection outcome, attaching evidence, requiring inspection before
disposition.

Out. Repair work. Supplier quality claims.

Design notes

An inspection step that can be completed with one tap is not an inspection. Under time
pressure everything passes, and the outcome is identical to having no inspection at all —
except now there is an audit trail saying it was checked, which is worse.

Three things make it real:

- Require a condition grade, not a yes/no.
- Require a reason for anything other than "as new".
- Report pass rates by inspector. An inspector passing 100% is not inspecting.

Verify identity, not just condition. Customers return the wrong product surprisingly often.
Scan it rather than trusting the RMA line.

RET-303 is the gate. Disposition cannot proceed without an inspection record. Enforce it
in the service layer.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Inspection is a rubber stamp | [doc 09 §8.2](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Damaged stock restocked | [doc 09 §8.1](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Wrong product returned and not detected | [doc 05 WF 9](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
